We can predict volcanic eruptions in the short term when volcanoes are well monitored, but we cannot reliably predict the exact timing or magnitude of eruptions, nor can we predict eruptions years in advance. Short-term predictions are feasible for instrumented volcanoes, yet global forecasting success is low and many eruptions lack clear precursors. Forecasting provides probabilistic estimates rather than definitive predictions, and no tool exists to definitively say when a specific volcano will erupt. These differing outcomes reflect conflicting opinions and research outcomes in volcanology.
